## Scope of the evidence (and its hard limits)

I was given only **mean |IG| magnitudes** — no sign, no per-cell values, no subgroup statistics, no conditional logic (this is the IG-ONLY ablation). Two features of the *feature space itself* also constrain what could have been learned, and I flag them honestly because they bound my confidence:

1. **PTPRC is absent from the feature list.** There is no total-CD45 RNA feature, no CD45 isoform-specific transcript, and no known PTPRC variable-exon splicing regulators (PTBP1, hnRPLL, SRSF/hnRNP family). Classic naive-T markers (CCR7, TCF7, LEF1, SELL, IL7R, CD3D/E, CD4, CD27, CD28) are also absent. The model therefore *could not* have learned a direct cis/trans regulatory mechanism — it must predict CD45RA protein from state/lineage surrogates.
2. **~40% of the top-100 features are MOUSE_ genes** (Neat1 #15, Gnb2 #23, Rpl8 #26, Cald1 #29, H3f3b #33, Cox/OXPHOS, ribosomal, cytoskeletal genes). Mouse transcripts cannot regulate a human protein; their substantial attribution implies the training data contain non-human cells (or a concatenated multi-dataset matrix) carrying no human CD45RA signal. This is a **species/composition axis, not CD45RA biology**, and it should be QC'd out before mechanistic interpretation. Relatedly, the stated study tissue ("CD45RA+ naive T cells") is inconsistent with the lineage breadth implied by the ranking (strong monocyte, B, erythroid, platelet, and mouse signals) — the model appears trained on a full-PBMC-like mixture. I cannot resolve this discrepancy from the given evidence.

## Rationale and single best hypothesis

CD45RA is a *protein isoform* of PTPRC generated by alternative splicing (inclusion of variable exon 4), not a gene whose RNA is in the feature space. The ranking shows the model predicts it from **cell-state and lineage codes**:

**Hypothesis:** CD45RA surface abundance in this dataset is not controlled by any single upstream transcript; it is entrained to **lymphocyte differentiation state and lineage identity via activation-coupled alternative splicing of PTPRC (the CD45RA→CD45RO switch)**. The cytotoxic NK/CD8 program ranks highest because it is the best available (inverse) surrogate for the naive state within the T-cell compartment, where the RA→RO switch occurs; the monocyte program ranks next because monocytes are CD45RO-biased; the B program contributes because B cells express RA-epitope-bearing CD45 isoforms. Because NK cells and CD8 Temra cells express the cytotoxic program while remaining CD45RA+, I further predict the model uses these features with **sign heterogeneity** (negative in central/effector-memory T cells, positive/neutral in NK and Temra) — which would inflate their mean |IG| and explain why they dominate this magnitude-only ranking.

**Testable predictions:**
1. Per-cell signed IG, or per-lineage expression-vs-ADT correlation, will show GNLY/NKG7/GZMA/CMC1 attributions are **negative in CD8 Tcm/Tem** but positive/neutral in NK and Temra; CST3/LYZ/CD14/S100A12 uniformly negative; IGHM/CD79A/MS4A1/TCL1A uniformly positive.
2. Adding PTPRC total RNA or exon-4-inclusion (isoform-level) features should **displace the cytotoxic cluster** from the top of the ranking (i.e., it is a proxy for isoform state).
3. TCR stimulation of sorted naive CD45RA+ T cells should induce the cytotoxic program while losing CD45RA (established); perturbing PTPRC splicing regulators (PTBP1, hnRPLL) should **decouple** cytotoxic-gene induction from CD45RA loss, distinguishing splicing-mediated regulation from correlative state tracking.

## (a) or (b)?

Primarily **(a) — direct confirmation of established knowledge**: CD45RA defines naive T cells and is lost in favor of CD45RO upon priming (Sanders, Makgoba & Shaw, *J Immunol* 1988; Akbar et al., *Nature* 1988); PTPRC variable-exon splicing is activation-regulated (Lynch & Weiss, *Mol Cell Biol* 2000; reviewed in Hermiston, Xu & Weiss, *Annu Rev Immunol* 2003); monocytes are CD45RO-biased and B cells carry RA-epitope isoforms. (I cite these from memory and cannot verify bibliographic details here; the PTBP1/hnRPLL splicing-regulator literature is from the Lynch lab and colleagues.) The **(b) element — new and testable** — is the sign-heterogeneity prediction for the cytotoxic program across NK/Temra vs. memory T cells, and the proxy-displacement prediction; neither is established in the literature and both are falsifiable with this same dataset plus signed attributions or isoform-aware features.

## Ablation-specific takeaway

The raw IG ranking **already recovers the dominant biological axes** (cytotoxic-effector state; myeloid and B lineage composition), so the classifier stage is not needed to identify *what* matters. What the raw ranking cannot provide is *direction, context-dependence, and subgroup logic* — those require the classifier/per-cell signed attributions. A large fraction of the top signal (the mouse-gene block) is a species/composition axis that should be removed before biological interpretation. To go further I would need: signed per-cell IG or per-lineage expression–ADT correlations; PTPRC total/isoform-level features; and metadata clarifying dataset composition (human/mouse; sorted vs. full PBMC) and the discrepancy with the stated study tissue.
